action.question: How should `sessions submit` know the sender's `cse_*` id to embed?

questions.question: How should `sessions submit` know the sender's `cse_*` id to embed?

options.label: Auto-detect from env (Recommended)
options.description: Read $CLAUDE_SESSION_ID (or whatever the running claude exposes); fall back to --reply-to if missing. Caller-free in the common case.

options.label: Required --reply-to flag
options.description: Always explicit. Caller must pass --reply-to cse_XXX. Simplest, but the skill has to add a step to fetch the agent's own id every time.

options.label: Optional --reply-to flag, no auto-detect
options.description: Off by default; only embeds when caller passes the flag. Least magic, but easy to forget.

questions.question: How should the sender-id be embedded in the message body?

options.label: Prepend a one-line header (Recommended)
options.description: Prefix the body with `[from cse_XXX — reply via send-to-session]\n\n<message>`. Visible to the receiving agent, parse-friendly for future tooling.

options.label: Append a footer
options.description: Same content but at the end. Less likely to throw off the receiving model's read of the prompt.

options.label: Both header and footer
options.description: Belt-and-braces; the id is hard to miss but the body gets noisier.

transcript_tail.text: the sendmessage should post the reply to session id

The recent commit said the receiver must reply via the same skill, but the receiver currently has to guess or ask for the sender's `cse_*` id (skill doc step 1). You want the `submit` CLI to embed the sender's session id in the body itself so the receiver always knows where to reply.

Before I edit anything, two design choices:

expected.rec_session: Auto-detect from env (Recommended), Prepend a one-line header (Recommended)
